definitions.gloss: sidelong glance; looking out of the corner of one's eye
definitions.explanation: The act of looking at something or someone from the side without turning one's head, often implying suspicion, jealousy, or discreet observation.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}を{横目|よこめ}で{見|み}た。
examples.english: I glanced at her out of the corner of my eye.

examples.japanese: {隣|となり}の{人|ひと}のテストを{横目|よこめ}で{見|み}てはいけない。
examples.english: You must not peek at your neighbor's test from the corner of your eye.

examples.japanese: {周|まわ}りの{騒|さわ}ぎを{横目|よこめ}に、{彼|かれ}は{黙々|もくもく}と{仕事|しごと}を{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: Paying no attention to the commotion around him, he silently continued working.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used in the patterns {横目|よこめ}で{見|み}る (to glance sideways at) and {横目|よこめ}に (while ignoring; with a sidelong glance at). The pattern ～を{横目|よこめ}に means to observe something peripherally while focusing on something else, often implying indifference.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {横目|よこめ}で{見|み}る (to look at sideways)
- ～を{横目|よこめ}に (paying no attention to ~; while glancing at ~)
- {横目|よこめ}を{使|つか}う (to use a sidelong glance)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {流|なが}し{目|め}: a lingering sidelong glance — often flirtatious
- ちらっと{見|み}る: to take a quick peek — briefer and less deliberate
- にらむ: to glare at — hostile and direct, not sideways
